title: A regional note, from script to report

steps.say: Start with the header and a setup chunk. The top of analysis.R moves in almost unchanged; include: false keeps it off the page.
The summary is written once, with every number inline. The chart gets a label, a size, and a caption and alt text that follow REGION; R writes the alt text's numbers too.
The second figure is two charts in two columns. fig-subcap names each panel and fig-alt describes it; fig-cap names the whole figure.
Add the table and a folded method note, and point to every figure and table from the summary.
The done test: change REGION, render, and every number, caption and chart moves. Nothing in the text was typed by hand.

final:
---
title: "Unemployment in one region"
subtitle: "Synthetic data, for training only"
date: today
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    embed-resources: true
execute:
  echo: false
---


```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tinytable)
rates <- read_csv("unemployment.csv")
REGION <- "Tabuk"
area    <- rates |> filter(region == REGION)
kingdom <- rates |> filter(region == "Kingdom")
now  <- last(area$rate)
then <- first(area$rate)
gap  <- now - last(kingdom$rate)
```

## Summary

In `r REGION` the rate was
`r scales::number(now, accuracy = 0.1)`% in 2025 Q4,
`r scales::number(now - then, accuracy = 0.1, style_positive = "plus")`
points since 2022 Q1 and
`r scales::number(gap, accuracy = 0.1, style_positive = "plus")`
points against the Kingdom (@fig-trend, @fig-compare, @tbl-recent).

## Trend

```{r}
#| label: fig-trend
#| fig-cap: !expr str_glue("Unemployment rate, {REGION} (%)")
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-alt: !expr str_glue(
#|   "Line chart of the unemployment rate",
#|   " in {REGION} by quarter, from {then}%",
#|   " in 2022 Q1 to {now}% in 2025 Q4.")
ggplot(area, aes(date, rate)) + geom_line()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-compare
#| fig-cap: "Against the Kingdom"
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-subcap: ["Both series", "The last four quarters"]
#| fig-alt: !expr c(
#|   str_glue("Line chart of the rate by quarter in",
#|     " {REGION} and the Kingdom, one colour each."),
#|   str_glue("Bar chart of each quarter of 2025",
#|     ", {REGION}'s bar beside the Kingdom's."))
both <- rates |> filter(region %in% c(REGION, "Kingdom"))
ggplot(both, aes(date, rate, colour = region)) +
  geom_line()
both |>
  filter(quarter >= "2025Q1") |>
  ggplot(aes(quarter, rate, fill = region)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge")
```

## Latest quarters

```{r}
#| label: tbl-recent
#| tbl-cap: !expr str_glue("Unemployment rate, {REGION} (%)")
area |>
  select(quarter, rate) |>
  slice_tail(n = 4) |>
  tt() |>
  theme_html(portable = TRUE)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Method"}
Rates are the unemployed as a share of the labour force.
The data are synthetic, made for training.
:::
